extracted.intended_audience: Early-career researchers preparing MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship (MSCA-PF) applications (e.g., NTNU applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing Part B of MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship proposals: demonstrating excellence, impact, and quality of implementation (workplan, risks, dissemination, IP, communication, career development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific achievements and broader professional accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific achievements (patents, university prizes, scholarships, industrial research experience, etc.). At this early career stage, no (reasonably recent) award is too small to mention!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List patents, prizes, scholarships, industrial experience, travel grants, best poster prizes. Also highlight international network/collaborations, previous activities demonstrating independent thinking (development of project ideas/new methods), leadership (teaching, mentoring, organising workshops), and management (project/lab management). 'Don’t run the risk of only describing your publication record! The point is to show that you are a well-rounded individual and professionally mature for your career stage.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit linkage of background to project suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: While describing your past achievements, you need to make it explicitly clear how your background makes you ideally suited to carry out the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how existing scientific and technical know-how provides a solid base to achieve project objectives; explain how any 'gaps' will be covered by the host; mention transferable skills (leadership, management, communication) that ensure smooth execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Impact (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Impact" essentially means any positive effect (benefit) that your results will have in the short or long term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a service attitude and tailor arguments to the goals of the funding scheme (read 'expected impact' in MSCA workprogramme). Think who/what benefits and why evaluators should invest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility of measures to enhance career perspectives and employability (Section 2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: At a minimum, address specific measures to enhance career perspectives and employability of the researcher inside and/or outside academia and the expected contribution of proposed skills development to the future career of the researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain career aims (5–10 years), articulate alternative career paths (academic and non-academic), describe how project contributes to new research and transferable skills, be realistic given the fellowship timeframe, and identify weaknesses/gaps to be addressed. Mention mandatory Career Development Plan (deliverable at month 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested content for career development (concrete skills & activities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the project contributes to a set of new skills/competences (both research skills and transferable skills) and how these skills will help you to achieve your career aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about courses, training, career development programs at host and external training. Examples: learning new research methods/applications; widening international network/collaborations; training in supervision skills; lecturing; applying for funding. TIPs: explain supervisor/host support for networking; if aiming for independence, include supervision and leadership training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for dissemination, exploitation and communication (Section 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the planned measures to maximize the impact of your project by providing a first version of your 'plan for the dissemination and exploitation including communication activities'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe dissemination/exploitation measures, target groups (scientific community, end users, financial actors, public), communication/public engagement strategy (main messages, tools, channels). Activities should be strategic, start at outset and continue through project lifetime. State objectives and timeline and include main dissemination/communication events in the Gantt chart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy for management of intellectual property (IP)
rubrics_metrics.description: If relevant, discuss the strategy for the management of intellectual property, foreseen protection measures (patents, design rights, copyright, trade secrets, etc.), and how these would be used to support exploitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe IP protection measures and follow-up beyond project lifetime; present an adequate IPR strategy regarding authorship/copyright and how planned open publishing will enhance impact. If IPR is not relevant, state and justify why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish dissemination, exploitation and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Dissemination: disclosure of results to stakeholder groups to enable them to use the results. Exploitation: use of results during and after the project (commercial or policy, etc.). Communication: strategic promotion of project and results to multiple audiences including the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think about target audience and direct relevance: dissemination targets those likely to implement results; communication targets broader public and aims to raise interest/understanding and show how EU funding benefits society. Always start with the four questions: Why? Who? What? How?

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe how results will be used (exploitation examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how project results will be used (i.e. exploited) to maximize impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include making results publicly available (if no IPR/data restrictions); use in further internal research and education; commercialisation (products/processes, licensing, spin-offs); providing services; use in standardisation activities. Link exploitation to dissemination strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete dissemination activities and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the planned dissemination activities (be specific).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give topic, target journal/conference and timing, explain why chosen, be realistic about number of publications. Other activities: presentations at international conferences, project website, social media, podcasts, magazines. If possible, define KPIs (e.g. audience size) and include events in the Gantt chart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and public outreach strategy (concrete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate a communication and public outreach strategy containing intermediate and final communication aims and deadlines, target groups, and how messages will be adapted to non-specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify planned one-way (press, radio, TV, posters, video) and two-way activities (dialogues/workshops/group discussions, school visits, open days), include user-engagement and co-creation processes, emphasize involvement of scientific and non-scientific audiences, and include main communication events in Gantt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify target groups and expected reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify who has an interest in your research, who can contribute to your work, who would be affected, and who could influence elsewhere; define expected types of reactions (feedback/dialogue, influence decision-makers, trigger action, uptake to production).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about target groups (policy makers, decision makers, school children, special public groups) and tailor messages and channels accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative of expected scientific, societal and economic impacts (Section 2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a narrative explaining how the project's results are expected to make a difference in terms of impact beyond the project's immediate scope and duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific and refer to target groups. Describe expected scientific impacts (contributing to advances, new knowledge, infrastructures), economic/technological impacts (new products/services, efficiency, standards), societal impacts (e.g. CO2 reduction, improved policies, health). Only include impacts where the project makes a significant and direct contribution. Provide quantified estimates where possible and meaningful. If basic research with long-term societal/economic impacts, explain why not relevant now. TIP: relate to UN SDGs, Horizon priorities, IPCC, directives, industrial challenges where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convince feasibility: Quality & Efficiency of Implementation (Section 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that your research is realistic in terms of scope, scale, time and money, that you have planned for unexpected events (risks), and that you can meet research and training objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe project management, progress monitoring, handling of problems, compliance with ethical and legal standards, and include other organisations involved (secondments, non-academic placements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Workplan structure, deliverables and milestones (3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief presentation of the overall structure of the work plan, including deliverables and milestones; timing of the different work packages and their components; mechanisms in place to assess and mitigate risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an overview (e.g. number of WPs, tasks, D/M), describe chronologically how project will progress, align WPs with objectives, ensure deliverables/milestones are appropriate and informative. Use 2–3 scientific WPs for a two-year project, with 1–3 deliverables and 1 milestone per WP as a guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gantt chart requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Gantt chart must be included and should indicate the proposed Work Packages (WP), major deliverables, milestones, secondments, placements. The schedule should indicate the number of months elapsed from the start of the action (Month 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gantt counts toward the 10-page limit. Ensure Gantt perfectly aligns with the proposed work plan and references training, communication and dissemination activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: Work Packages, Deliverables, Milestones, Risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Work Packages: sub-projects aimed to achieve objectives. Deliverables: specific outputs (tangible or intangible). Milestones: 'checkpoints' enabling monitoring and corrective measures. Risks: events that may delay or endanger completion of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose deliverables corresponding to important expected results (not just 'a publication'); milestones should be critical rate-limiting steps. Identify scientific/administrative risks and explain mitigation so evaluators are confident objectives remain feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory and recommended deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three mandatory Deliverables for all MSCA-PF projects: 1) Data management plan (Month 6), 2) Career development plan (Month 6), 3) Communication, Dissemination and Outreach Plan (month before project end).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, include 1–2 scientific deliverables per scientific WP, well spread out. Ensure deliverables correspond to important outputs and are timed logically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing, allocation of resources and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the timing of Work Packages and their duration and justify allocation of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight resources that facilitate tasks (established techniques, prior experience, technical support). Explain feasibility of overlapping WPs. Mention important in-kind contributions from host and justify that objectives are achievable within available budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress monitoring and risk mitigation (practical plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how you will manage your project, monitor progress, and deal with problems; go through each WP and identify critical risks and mitigation measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use meetings (weekly supervisory, quarterly reviews), set milestones to monitor progress, present a risk table listing likelihood, consequence, and mitigation. Describe institutional support (EU research advisors, legal/financial experts). Present mitigation measures both in table and narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and labelling for coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Label your deliverables, milestones and risks (e.g. D1.1) and make them visible in the narrative to ensure coherence between sections of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference deliverables/milestones/risks between methodology, dissemination and workplan sections so evaluators can track coherence. TIP: be realistic; over-ambition undermines feasibility.
